subtitle: When Ashes Became a Map of Power

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide, like a painted mural come alive
panels.action: Dona, Keeper of the Relics, stands between a smouldering funeral pyre and a ring of stern envoys from distant republics and kingdoms, his hands resting on a great urn as the dawn mist hangs over Kusinara’s trees.

dialogue.text: After the Buddha’s passing, eight powers faced a single urn of relics—Dona the brahmin stood between war and ash.

i18n.hi: बुद्ध के निर्वाण के बाद, आठ शक्तियाँ एक कलश पर भिड़ीं—ब्राह्मण दोणा खड़े थे युद्ध और राख के बीच।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the still-glowing funeral pyre at Kusinara
panels.action: The cremation ground outside Kusinara shows a great pyre collapsing into embers, monks in simple robes standing in silent rows, while Dona watches from the edge, his face lit by the last tongues of flame.

dialogue.text: At Kusinara, under sal trees, the Teacher’s body was burned. When the fire died, bone and ash remained—silent, heavy with claim.

i18n.hi: कुशीनगर में, साल के पेड़ों तले, भगवा देह जली। आग बुझी तो बस अस्थि और राख बची—चुप, पर दावे से भारी।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Dona examining the relics beside monks
panels.action: Dona kneels beside the monks, carefully lifting pale fragments from the cooled embers with a metal ladle into a large urn, the forest beyond hazy and still.

dialogue.text: The brahmin Dona, versed in rites and order, gathered the relics into an urn. In the Pali chronicle, he is named the mediator of what came next.

i18n.hi: विधि–विद्वान ब्राह्मण दोणा ने अवशेष एक कलश में समेटे।पाली ग्रंथ उन्हें आगे की बात का मध्यस्थ कहता है।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Kusinara’s gate road, dusty and busy
panels.action: Envoys from different lands arrive along a dirt road toward Kusinara: some in republican cloaks with spears and standards, some in royal chariots, while farmers and villagers stare at the sudden traffic.

dialogue.text: Word ran swift along the Ganga plain. From republics and monarchies alike, envoys rode to Kusinara, each carrying a claim to the bones of the Awakened One.

i18n.hi: गंगा के मैदान में खबर बिजली-सी दौड़ी। गणों और राजाओं से दूत कुशीनगर दौड़े, सबके हाथ में जाग्रत के अस्थियों का दावा।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of a gathering hall filled with delegations
panels.action: Inside a large wooden hall of the Mallas, eight delegations face one another: Mallas of Kusinara and Pava, Licchavis of Vesali, Shakyas, Koliyas, a dignified brahmin from Vethadipa, Moriyas, and a stately Magadhan envoy, while Dona stands near the urn at the centre.

dialogue.text: The Digha Nikaya names eight claimants: Mallas of Kusinara, Mallas of Pava, Licchavis, Shakyas, Koliyas of Ramagama, a brahmin of Vethadipa, Moriyas of Pipphalivana, and Ajatashatru of Magadha.

i18n.hi: दीर्घ निकाय आठ दावेदार गिनता है—कुशीनगर के मल्ल, पावा के मल्ल, लिच्छवि, शाक्य, रामग्राम के कोलिय, वेथदीप का ब्राह्मण, पिप्फलिवन के मौर्य और मगध का अजातशत्रु।

panels.shot: medium shot of two delegates arguing across the hall
panels.action: A Kusinara Malla councillor and a Licchavi envoy stand facing each other, hands raised in argument, while others murmur; Dona watches, jaw set, his hand still resting on the urn.

dialogue.speaker: Licchavi Envoy
dialogue.text: The Teacher walked our streets in Vesali. We too have right.

i18n.hi: आचार्य हमारे वैशाली में चले। हमारा भी हक है।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Dona’s thoughtful, lined face
panels.action: Beads of sweat stand on Dona’s brow as he looks from one angry face to another, a faint reflection of the urn shimmering in his eyes.

dialogue.text: Tradition remembers tempers flaring, voices rising. Over sacred bone, the old rivalries of the middle Ganga plain breathed again.

i18n.hi: परंपरा कहती है, गुस्सा भड़का, आवाजें गरजीं। पवित्र अस्थियों पर गंगा–मध्यम के पुराने बैर फिर जाग उठे।

panels.shot: medium shot as Dona steps forward, hand raised
panels.action: Dona steps between the factions, right hand raised for silence, left hand still touching the urn, the smoke-stained hall lit by afternoon light.

dialogue.speaker: Dona, Keeper of the Relics
dialogue.text: If you quarrel over him, what will his relics teach?

i18n.hi: अगर तुम उन्हीं पर लड़ोगे, तो उनकी अस्थियाँ क्या सिखाएँगी?

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Dona toward the envoys
panels.action: From behind Dona’s shoulder, the envoys are seen listening, some arms still folded, others softening, the urn looming at the edge of the frame.

dialogue.text: The sutta’s coda preserves only the outcome, not his arguments. Later scholars read in it a delicate diplomacy rather than simple piety.

i18n.hi: सूत्र का अंत बस नतीजा बचाता है, तर्क नहीं। बाद के विद्वान इसमें नर्म कूटनीति देखते हैं, केवल भक्ति नहीं।

panels.shot: symbolic cutaway: map-like view of the middle Ganga plain
panels.action: A stylised overhead view shows rivers and small city-states—Kusinara, Vesali, Kapilavastu, Ramagama, Pipphalivana, Magadha—each marked by modest walls and assembly halls rather than huge palaces.

dialogue.text: Across the middle Ganga plain, small gana-sanghas and monarchies jostled. Sharing relics meant sharing prestige—each stupa a quiet claim of place in a new moral order.

i18n.hi: मध्य गंगा–मैदान में छोटे गण-संघ और राजघराने ठेलते–धकियाते थे। अवशेष बाँटना था यश बाँटना—हर स्तूप एक चुप दावा, नई धारणा–व्यवस्था में जगह का।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dona with simple measuring tools beside the urn
panels.action: Dona sits on a woven mat before the urn with a set of simple measuring bowls and trays, monks and envoys watching as he prepares to apportion the relics.

dialogue.text: Dona proposed division. One urn of bones, eight powers. The chronicle says he measured carefully, not favouring Kusinara over distant Pipphalivana or mighty Magadha.

i18n.hi: दोणा ने बँटवारा सुझाया। एक कलश, आठ शक्तियाँ। ग्रंथ कहता है, उसने नाप–तौल कर बाँटा—न कुशीनगर को तराज़ू झुकाया, न दूर पिप्फलिवन या शक्तिशाली मगध को।

panels.shot: close-up of Dona’s hands as he portions relics into smaller vessels
panels.action: Dona’s hands gently scoop fragments into eight smaller vessels laid out in a circle, each a different shape and ornament, while the larger urn remains half-full beside them.

dialogue.text: He divided the relics into eight shares. Later Buddhist communities would see in this act the seed of a far-reaching network of stupas.

i18n.hi: उसने अवशेष आठ हिस्सों में बाँटे। बाद के बौद्ध समुदायों ने इसी में दूर-दूर तक फैलते स्तूप–जाल का बीज देखा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dona lifting the emptying urn with quiet resolve
panels.action: As the eight vessels sit filled, Dona cradles the original urn against his chest, looking at it with a sense of attachment and thought, the envoys watching curiously.

dialogue.text: Yet the story adds another strand: Dona kept the urn itself. The text remembers that, besides the bones, the vessel and even the embers received their own honours.

i18n.hi: पर कहानी एक और तंतु जोड़ती है—कलश खुद दोणा ने रख लिया। ग्रंथ याद रखता है कि अस्थियों के साथ पात्र और चिंगारियों तक को अलग सम्मान मिला।

panels.shot: wide shot of envoys carrying their relic vessels out of Kusinara
panels.action: Each delegation departs along different roads, carefully bearing their relic vessel: a Licchavi caravan, a small Shakya group, the Magadhan escort with disciplined lines of guards.

dialogue.text: From Kusinara, relics fanned out. Vesali, Kapilavastu, Ramagama, Pipphalivana, Magadha—all would, tradition says, raise mounds over their share, binding territory to memory.

i18n.hi: कुशीनगर से अवशेष फैल गए—वैशाली, कपिलवस्तु, रामग्राम, पिप्फलिवन, मगध—सबने, परंपरा कहती है, अपने हिस्से पर टीले उठाए, भूमि को स्मृति से बाँधा।

panels.shot: cutaway montage: early stupas rising in different landscapes
panels.action: A montage shows simple earthen stupas being heaped and plastered in different settings—near forests, beside rivers, within city outskirts—with villagers and monks working together.

dialogue.text: Archaeology has glimpsed only fragments of this world—like early stupas at Vesali and the unexcavated mound at Ramagrama—yet the coda’s list still sketches a political map of faith.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्व को इस जगत की बस झलकें मिलीं—जैसे वैशाली के प्राचीन स्तूप, और रामग्राम का अनखुदा टीला—फिर भी इस अंत–सूची से आस्था का राजनीतिक नक्शा झलकता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dona overseeing a small stupa being raised over the urn
panels.action: Back near Kusinara, Dona watches artisans pile bricks over the original urn itself, shaping a modest stupa while monks chant softly nearby.

dialogue.text: Over the urn and even the embers, memorial mounds were raised. The sutta’s final lines note them almost briefly, yet they mark how ritual, relic, and landscape fused.

i18n.hi: कलश पर, यहाँ तक कि चूल्हे की राख पर भी स्मृति–टीलों का निर्माण हुआ।सूत्र की अंतिम पंक्तियाँ इसे यूँ ही कह जाती हैं, पर वहीं दिखता है जहाँ विधि, अवशेष और भू-दृश्य घुल गए।

panels.shot: reflective close-up of Dona in later years, seated by a stupa
panels.action: An older Dona sits in the shade near a finished stupa, watching pilgrims circle it in quiet devotion, his hands folded loosely in his lap.

dialogue.text: Later generations would argue over dates and layers of the text, asking if this coda is early or late. But their debates still return to Dona’s quiet role.

i18n.hi: बाद की पीढ़ियाँ तारीखों और परतों पर भिड़ीं—यह अंत पुराना है या नया? पर उनकी बहस फिर लौटती है दोणा की शांत भूमिका पर।

panels.shot: wide, almost timeless shot: the stupa silhouetted against the sky
panels.action: A stupa rises against a wide sky at dusk; pilgrims move like small shadows around its base, while distant hills fade into haze.

dialogue.text: In his measured hands, sacred relics became instruments of negotiation. Through him, memory itself was shared, and the Buddha’s passing drew rival polities into a fragile circle of common honour.

i18n.hi: उनके तौले हाथों में पावन अवशेष संधि के औज़ार बने। उन्हीं के ज़रिये स्मृति बाँटी गई, और बुद्ध का परिनिर्वाण प्रतिद्वंद्वी गण–राज्यों को साझा सम्मान के नाज़ुक घेरे में खींच लाया।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Ashes Became a Map of Power
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब राख बनी शक्ति का नक्शा
